channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: In planning family and careers, young Sikh American women say balancing act is their own
item.description: A new study challenges 'the assumption that being a good Sikh woman means following a single prescribed path,' said the researcher behind the findings.

item.title: Conservative Anglican bishops seek ‘disengagement’ from Canterbury without naming rival leader
item.description: Weeks before the first female archbishop of Canterbury is installed, the group of prelates known as GAFCON elected leaders to exercise 'principled disengagement' from the historic center of Anglicanism in England.

item.title: The Deepak Chopra-Jeffrey Epstein friendship tells of a spirituality industry in crisis
item.description: Chopra’s friendship with Epstein is dismaying, in part for what it says about the spiritual and wellness culture he exemplifies.

item.title: Israeli family who buried 3 of their children after missile attack clings to faith
item.description: They were among nine people killed Sunday when an Iranian missile strike demolished a synagogue and homes in Beit Shemesh.

item.title: 4 men arrested in UK on suspicion of aiding Iran by spying on Jewish community
item.description: Police said the men arrested are aged 22, 40, 52 and 55 and that searches are ongoing.

item.title: ‘A lie from the pit of hell’: Episcopal leaders push back on rumors of fatal decline
item.description: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (RNS) — More than 850 Episcopal Church leaders gathered in Charlotte to talk about the future of the church and what the denomination still has to offer.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV taps career Vatican diplomat Archbishop Caccia as representative to the US
item.description: Caccia, the Holy See's observer at the United Nations since 2019, replaces Cardinal Christophe Pierre as papal nuncio.

item.title: The Downward Arc of Donald Trump, With Ruth Ben-Ghiat
item.description: An expert on authoritarianism explains the ways strongmen consolidate power - and how they lose it

item.title: Closing Al-Aqsa Mosque during Ramadan sets a dangerous precedent
item.description: Muslims fear that Israel, which said the closure was over security, will misuse the situation to further tighten the Israeli police grip on the mosque and its management.

item.title: Deportations surge, aid collapses and faith groups in Latin America struggle to respond
item.description: 'There simply isn’t enough capacity even for the local community. It’s much harder with a population that has been abandoned in places that are extremely difficult,' said Karen Perez, the country director for Jesuit Refugee Service in Mexico.
